title: Checkout: retry storm
summary: Review: three stacked retry layers turn a slow payment provider into a 64x call storm; one retry layer plus idempotency keys contains it.

steps.title: Checkout must hold p99 < 400 ms at 1,500 orders/s
body: A marketplace checkout: write the order, charge the card, publish OrderPlaced. The targets that matter here are the given peak of 1,500 orders/s and p99 under 400 ms.

steps.title: One order, one charge, on the happy path
body: Client calls the gateway, the order service writes the row to Postgres, charges the card and publishes to Kafka. When the provider is healthy each order makes one charge call: 1,500 calls/s at peak.

steps.title: Three retry layers multiply, they do not add
body: Client, gateway and order service each retry 3 times, so each layer makes up to 4 attempts. Stacked, one checkout can reach the provider 4 x 4 x 4 = 64 times (derived from the Design section).

callout.text: The 'Gateway retries' row prices this as latency only. It is an amplifier.

steps.title: A slow provider gets 96,000 calls a second
body: The provider slows past the timeouts. Every layer sees failures and retries: 1,500 orders/s x 64 = 96,000 calls/s at the provider, which rate-limits or falls over. Order-service threads wait on it, the pool fills, and checkout p99 blows past 400 ms.

steps.title: A timed-out charge that succeeded is charged again
body: A timeout does not mean the charge failed. The doc sends no idempotency key, so each retry of a charge the provider already accepted is a new charge: up to 64 for one cart. Money moves twice; refunds and support follow.
changes: ~ double charges 0 -> possible on every timeout

steps.title: Retry in one place only: 64 -> 4 calls per order
body: Only the order service retries the provider (3 retries, jittered backoff). The gateway does not retry; the client does not resend on 5xx but polls the order status. Worst case falls to 1,500 x 4 = 6,000 calls/s.

callout.text: Cost: a slow charge now surfaces to the user as 'processing' instead of being hidden by retries.

steps.title: One key per order: a retry can never charge twice
body: The order service sends the order id as the provider's idempotency key on every attempt, so a retried charge returns the first result instead of charging again.

callout.text: Cost: the key must be stored with the order and reused across restarts; the provider's key window bounds how late a retry may come.

steps.title: Same boxes, one retry layer, no double charges
body: Steady state: 1,500 charge calls/s, worst case 6,000/s when the provider struggles instead of 96,000, and every charge is idempotent. Other findings (outbox for Kafka, DB-backed liveness probe, nightly backups vs RPO 1 min) are in the review log.
